<description>
The secp256k1 subtree is built without our hardening flags: they are on `core_interface`, which the subtree does not use, so unless the compiler enables them by default its objects miss FORTIFY, the stack protector, stack clash protection and control flow protection. On aarch64 Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15, the three secp256k1 objects are the only ones in the build tree without the control flow property, so master's `bitcoind` has no `AArch64 feature` note.

This PR moves the flags back to a `hardening_interface` library, which `core_interface` links (reverting 77e553ab6a), and `cmake/secp256k1.cmake` passes the subtree those its C compiler accepts. The same build then shows `AArch64 feature: BTI, PAC, GCS` on `bitcoind`. The depends libraries still lack `-fcf-protection` (#30677, #30685).
</description>

<commits>
08bd06ccd4 build: pass hardening flags to secp256k1

The hardening flags are added to core_interface, which the secp256k1
subtree does not use: cmake/secp256k1.cmake passes it only the
sanitizer and APPEND_* flags. Its objects are therefore built without
_FORTIFY_SOURCE, -fstack-protector-all, -fstack-clash-protection,
-fcf-protection and -mbranch-protection, unless the compiler enables
them by default.

This also drops the control flow property from the binaries. The
linker marks an executable as BTI/PAC (aarch64) or IBT/SHSTK (x86_64)
enabled only when every object it links has the property. On aarch64
Ubuntu 26.04 with GCC 15, bitcoind built from master has no AArch64
feature property, and the secp256k1 objects are the only objects in
the build tree without it.

Move the hardening flags to a hardening_interface library, which
core_interface links, and pass its compile and link options to the
subtree in the same way as sanitize_interface. This brings back the
hardening_interface that was folded into core_interface in 77e553ab6a,
now that the flags have a second user.

The hardening flags are checked with the C++ compiler, and the subtree
is built with the C compiler. Check them again with the C compiler and
pass on only those it accepts, so that a C compiler rejecting one of
them cannot break the subtree's build. Each flag is checked together
with those accepted before it, because -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 alone fails
with -Werror where CFLAGS already define _FORTIFY_SOURCE, and dropping
it while keeping -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE would build secp256k1 without
FORTIFY at all.
</commits>

<patch>
diff --git a/cmake/secp256k1.cmake b/cmake/secp256k1.cmake
index c82f361aba..215ad171e7 100644
--- a/cmake/secp256k1.cmake
+++ b/cmake/secp256k1.cmake
@@ -3,6 +3,38 @@
 # file COPYING or https://opensource.org/license/mit/.
 
 enable_language(C)
+include(CheckCSourceCompiles)
+
+# The hardening flags are checked with the C++ compiler.
+# Drop those that the C compiler rejects. Each flag is checked together
+# with those accepted before it, as -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 needs the
+# -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE before it.
+function(filter_c_flags var)
+  cmake_parse_arguments(PARSE_ARGV 1 FCF "LINK" "" "")
+  set(flags ${${var}})
+  separate_arguments(flags)
+  set(result)
+  foreach(flag IN LISTS flags)
+    string(MAKE_C_IDENTIFIER "${flag}" id)
+    string(TOUPPER "${id}" id)
+    if(FCF_LINK)
+      set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE EXECUTABLE)
+      set(CMAKE_REQUIRED_LINK_OPTIONS ${result} ${flag} ${working_linker_werror_flag})
+      set(check_result C_LINKER_SUPPORTS_${id})
+    else()
+      set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE STATIC_LIBRARY)
+      list(JOIN result " " accepted)
+      set(CMAKE_REQUIRED_FLAGS "${accepted} ${flag} ${working_compiler_werror_flag}")
+      set(check_result C_SUPPORTS_${id})
+    endif()
+    check_c_source_compiles("int main(void) { return 0; }" ${check_result})
+    if(${check_result})
+      list(APPEND result ${flag})
+    endif()
+  endforeach()
+  list(JOIN result " " result)
+  set(${var} "${result}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+endfunction()
 
 function(add_secp256k1 subdir)
   message("")
@@ -27,13 +59,19 @@ function(add_secp256k1 subdir)
   endif()
   set(SECP256K1_BUILD_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
   include(GetTargetInterface)
-  # -fsanitize and related flags apply to both C++ and C,
+  # -fsanitize, hardening and related flags apply to both C++ and C,
   # so we can pass them down to libsecp256k1 as CFLAGS and LDFLAGS.
   get_target_interface(SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS "" sanitize_interface COMPILE_OPTIONS)
+  get_target_interface(secp256k1_hardening_cflags "" hardening_interface COMPILE_OPTIONS)
+  filter_c_flags(secp256k1_hardening_cflags)
+  string(STRIP "${SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS} ${secp256k1_hardening_cflags}" SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS)
   string(STRIP "${SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS} ${APPEND_CPPFLAGS}" SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS)
   string(STRIP "${SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS} ${APPEND_CFLAGS}" SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS)
   set(SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS ${SECP256K1_APPEND_CFLAGS} CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
   get_target_interface(SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS "" sanitize_interface LINK_OPTIONS)
+  get_target_interface(secp256k1_hardening_ldflags "" hardening_interface LINK_OPTIONS)
+  filter_c_flags(secp256k1_hardening_ldflags LINK)
+  string(STRIP "${SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS} ${secp256k1_hardening_ldflags}" SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS)
   string(STRIP "${SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS} ${APPEND_LDFLAGS}" SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS)
   set(SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS ${SECP256K1_APPEND_LDFLAGS} CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
   # We want to build libsecp256k1 with the most tested RelWithDebInfo configuration.
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index f521f03b49..c5cdf6e69f 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -528,10 +528,13 @@ try_append_cxx_flags("-fmacro-prefix-map=A=B" TARGET core_interface SKIP_LINK
 # -fstack-reuse=none for all gcc builds. (Only gcc understands this flag).
 try_append_cxx_flags("-fstack-reuse=none" TARGET core_interface)
 
+# Hardening flags. They are also passed to the secp256k1 subtree.
+add_library(hardening_interface INTERFACE)
+target_link_libraries(core_interface INTERFACE hardening_interface)
 if(MSVC)
-  try_append_linker_flag("/DYNAMICBASE" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("/HIGHENTROPYVA" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("/NXCOMPAT" TARGET core_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("/DYNAMICBASE" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("/HIGHENTROPYVA" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("/NXCOMPAT" TARGET hardening_interface)
 else()
 
   # _FORTIFY_SOURCE requires that there is some level of optimization,
@@ -545,38 +548,38 @@ else()
             }"
   )
   if(cxx_supports_fortify_source)
-    target_compile_options(core_interface INTERFACE
+    target_compile_options(hardening_interface INTERFACE
       -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE
       -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3
     )
   endif()
   unset(cxx_supports_fortify_source)
 
-  try_append_cxx_flags("-Wstack-protector" TARGET core_interface SKIP_LINK)
-  try_append_cxx_flags("-fstack-protector-all" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_cxx_flags("-fcf-protection=full" TARGET core_interface)
+  try_append_cxx_flags("-Wstack-protector" TARGET hardening_interface SKIP_LINK)
+  try_append_cxx_flags("-fstack-protector-all" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_cxx_flags("-fcf-protection=full" TARGET hardening_interface)
 
   if(MINGW)
     # stack-clash-protection is a no-op for Windows.
     # See https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=90458 for more details.
   else()
-    try_append_cxx_flags("-fstack-clash-protection" TARGET core_interface)
+    try_append_cxx_flags("-fstack-clash-protection" TARGET hardening_interface)
   endif()
 
   if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR STREQUAL "aarch64" OR CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR STREQUAL "arm64")
     if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Darwin")
-      try_append_cxx_flags("-mbranch-protection=bti" TARGET core_interface SKIP_LINK)
+      try_append_cxx_flags("-mbranch-protection=bti" TARGET hardening_interface SKIP_LINK)
     else()
-      try_append_cxx_flags("-mbranch-protection=standard" TARGET core_interface SKIP_LINK)
+      try_append_cxx_flags("-mbranch-protection=standard" TARGET hardening_interface SKIP_LINK)
     endif()
   endif()
 
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--enable-reloc-section" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--dynamicbase" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--nxcompat" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--high-entropy-va" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,relro" TARGET core_interface)
-  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,now" TARGET core_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--enable-reloc-section" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--dynamicbase" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--nxcompat" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,--high-entropy-va" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,relro" TARGET hardening_interface)
+  try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,now" TARGET hardening_interface)
   # TODO: This can be dropped once Bitcoin Core no longer supports
   #       NetBSD 10.0 or if upstream fix is backported.
   # NetBSD's dynamic linker ld.elf_so < 11.0 supports exactly 2
@@ -586,12 +589,12 @@ else()
   # - https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28724#issuecomment-2589347934
   # - https://mail-index.netbsd.org/tech-userlevel/2023/01/05/msg013666.html
   if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "NetBSD" AND CMAKE_SYSTEM_VERSION VERSION_LESS 11.0)
-    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,noseparate-code" TARGET core_interface)
+    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,noseparate-code" TARGET hardening_interface)
   else()
-    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,separate-code" TARGET core_interface)
+    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-z,separate-code" TARGET hardening_interface)
   endif()
   if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Darwin")
-    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-fixup_chains" TARGET core_interface)
+    try_append_linker_flag("-Wl,-fixup_chains" TARGET hardening_interface)
   endif()
 endif()
 

</patch>
